title: Make pauses safe and resumes exact, define stuck and failure handling, and fix the swarming defects
action: Adopt the L3 doctrine practices (per D2 and D4), translated, never pasted, each in the section that already owns its rule. Keep SKILL.md short (it loads on every swarm): it gets only the hard-rule stop line, the Reply line and one-line pointers; every other practice — the handoff fields and rules, resume triage, stuck, the failure table, pilot, user stop, CI-red triage — lives in swarming-reference.md. go-mode.md is in scope because it owns the Slice Loop, where the land-before-budget line belongs. Rust-side items (upstream trace relay, patch-id, rolling refill in the CLI) are Slice 2 — do not add them. Do NOT run bee dev regen (wave-barrier). swarming-reference.md: (1) 'Handoff JSON' gains fields verified (proof lines run so far), tree (clean or dirty:<paths>), key_files and gotchas, and two rules — finish the current atomic edit or back it out before writing the handoff; a worker with dirty edits commits them as `wip: <subject>` with the `cell: <id>` trailer, and whoever finishes the cell amends that commit into the one cell commit before the cap, so no wip commit survives into history. (2) 'Fresh-session handoff in full' gains a triage for each in-flight cell: capped since the handoff → run the completeness check; claimed with no live worker and no commit → unclaim, release, re-dispatch; a cell: or wip: commit exists but not capped → dispatch a fresh worker to finish it. (3) Step 6 Tend defines stuck: no side effect (a commit, a reservation renewal, a trace write) past the runtime expected at dispatch; the remedy is stop, unclaim, release, re-dispatch; status probes stay read-only. (4) 'Proof at finish and close' gains 'When CI goes red after merge': flake → one re-run; stale base → sync with main and re-prove; a failure in the diff's own code → a fix-first cell. SKILL.md: (5) under the rescue ladder a short failure table — BLOCKED for missing context → fresh dispatch with the context; HANDOFF → fresh dispatch from the handoff; provider error → the fallback_chain step; red or task miss → same role with the failing excerpt; silent death → unclaim and re-dispatch; after a second failed re-dispatch surface to the user; point to the never-move-on-red rule, do not restate it. (6) Hard rules: when two workers fail on the same root cause, stop dispatch, let in-flight work finish, open a fix-first cell, resume after it caps. (7) Orchestrate: a wave of same-role same-pattern cells dispatches one pilot first and fans out after it goal-checks; on a user stop, stop every live worker, keep the claims, write a pause handoff; end the Orchestrate section with a Reply line (capped over total, proof per cell, merge or uat state, blockers, the one next action). (8) Execute: before the commit, revert any edit the proof did not need; for green:live on a behavior-changing cell, the scope reason names the before-state seen on main. go-mode.md Slice Loop: (9) when the context budget is near its handoff point with slices left, cap and close the current slice first and open no new slice. DEFECTS: (10) worker-details.md: the commit example writes `-m "Cell: <cell-id>"`; change it to the literal lowercase `cell: <cell-id>`. (11) Give the Result form one home in swarming-reference.md and the departure rule one home in worker-details.md; the other places point there. Note: `bee finish` is a real alias of `bee cells finish` (verified), so do not rename it. Prefer words over a new numeric limit. Cite qualified pointers without the skills/ prefix.
